runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Six wins from six recent starts including four on Good going — her record is exceptional and Denis Hogan's yard (4/29 14-day) is ticking over; at OR 103 she carries the highest rating alongside Black Caviar Gold and is the standout form horse if she avoids the early prominent scrummage.
runners_data.comment: Meriden brings a blazing run of five consecutive wins into this, though her our rating of 98 sits a shade below her official mark, and she carries 129 lb from stall two; has run over today's trip and going, but our rating of 98 ranks her only sixth.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race prominently but is genuinely unlikely to secure that position given the surplus of prominent types in this field; her Good-ground form (2nd, 3rd) is solid but racing off a true rhythm will blunt her effectiveness here.
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Attack showed real promise with a third and a second in recent starts, and she has experience over today's trip and going; rated 109 by us, she shapes as a leading danger, though her fourth last time out raises questions about consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Celtic Motif is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 10-runner field, she will dictate from the front without serious pressure, likely settling into a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Galway over 7f. Celestial Orbit, La Brodeuse, Black Caviar Gold, and Meriden all want prominent positions and will jostle for the first three furlongs, creating a condensed pocket of traffic between the 2f and 3f markers that demands clean passage. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Noli Timere and Pivotal Attack are genuine front-runners by nature but are highly unlikely to secure their preferred position here given that congestion, and so both are mapped to midfield. With Celtic Motif controlling tempo at a fair but unspectacular clip, this race shape strongly favours hold-up and late-running profiles that can avoid the early scrimmaging and produce a sustained finish — closers who save ground, find a run, and sustain into the final 2f are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Celtic Motif Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Motif dictates a fair pace unchallenged and the prominent group gets shuffled into traffic, leaving the hold-up runners to sweep late.
scenarios.body: Celtic Motif sets a rhythm that suits those coming from off the pace, and the prominent congestion 2-3f out means closers bypass the trouble and hit the line with momentum. Hold-up types Greydreambeliever and Nancy J are perfectly positioned to exploit this shape, and Meriden's relentless winning streak means she could still pick her way through from a prominent-ish pitch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Meriden Dominates From Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Meriden secures an unobstructed prominent berth early and her exceptional recent form translates to this step up in class.
scenarios.body: Six consecutive wins including four on Good ground at 7f underlines her affinity for these conditions, and Chris Hayes will be able to slot in just behind Celtic Motif before quickening decisively 2f out. Her OR of 103 and flawless winning sequence make her the outstanding form horse if she travels smoothly through the early traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Two Draw Clear Early
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group get disrupted badly and Celtic Motif, joined by one fresh prominent mover, sets a strong enough pace to strand the field.
scenarios.body: If Celtic Motif quickens slightly and pulls Celestial Orbit or La Brodeuse along with her into a breakaway, the hold-up runners face too much ground to make up. Celestial Orbit won last time and has the class to sustain a prominent effort, while La Brodeuse's recent second on Good ground indicates she handles this surface racing handy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Blocked, Prominent Wins Messy
scenarios.trigger: If traffic chaos in the straight prevents the closers from threading through and a prominent type who avoids trouble lands a messy verdict.
scenarios.body: With four or five horses cramped across the track 2f out, a hold-up horse who finds no gap is simply eliminated, handing the race to whoever avoided the melee near the front. Black Caviar Gold has prior form at this sort of distance and surface from a handy position and could capitalise, with Pivotal Attack — though racing out of natural role — a slight beneficiary if she finds a gap.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Motif — if she quickens from the front at the 3f mark before the prominent pack has sorted itself, she could open an uncatchable gap; watch for J M Sheridan pressing the button early.

Traffic flashpoint between Celestial Orbit, La Brodeuse, Black Caviar Gold, and Meriden in the 3f-2f corridor — four horses competing for two berths is a near-certain recipe for interference, and any runner caught wide or checked here is effectively eliminated.

Noli Timere and Pivotal Attack — both natural front-runners rerouted to midfield; if either gets shuffled sideways on the turn into the straight, watch for their jockeys having to check or switch, compromising everyone around them.

Greydreambeliever — her hold-up profile is ideal for the dominant shape, but Declan McDonogh must navigate the traffic fallout from the prominent group cleanly; any check at the 2f marker will cost her the race.

Goldilocks Cen (unclassified style, 0 wins or places from 4 runs on Good) — monitor in the early stages to see whether she settles mid-pack or tries to stride on; her unpredictable positioning could add to the congestion problem.

races.name: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Steeplechase (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Shadow Paddy
runners_data.note: Five wins on Good turf including back-to-back wins at 17f and 20f make this his ideal conditions; Eoin McCarthy's yard is 1/14 in the T14 window but the horse's form speaks loudly, and as the sole genuine front-runner he controls the race shape entirely — only a jumping blunder could derail him.

runners_data.name: Court Canyon
runners_data.note: Won at 20f on Good last time out for Ian Donoghue's yard but is 87 days off the track; a naturally prominent-racing type who cannot secure his usual berth in this pace-heavy field and is mapped to midfield — he will need a trouble-free passage to reproduce his best.

runners_data.name: Le Coq Hardi
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old has won and finished second in his last two over 2m on Good ground, boasting the most consistent recent form profile in the field; Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride and this horse's 12-from-15 strike on similar going is the standout statistic — well-placed to chase Shadow Paddy with genuine intent.

runners_data.name: Soir De Garde
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's booking for Mullins is the eye-catching angle: the horse won last time at 16f on Good and has course-applicable form, but is a natural prominent runner whose redistribution to the rear in this crowded prominent field is against his grain — Townend may push forward regardless, making his actual position fluid.

runners_data.name: Wild Bill Hickok
runners_data.note: The youngest horse in the field at four, stepping up markedly from 16f to 2m2f for the first time; won twice at 16f on Good and his headgear note (hg:h) suggests he has needed managing — the extra distance is the key unknown and Eoghan Finegan will need to judge the pace carefully.

runners_data.name: Lady Bluebird
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old who won last time over 2m on Good, she is racing prominently by nature but is squeezed into a midfield slot by the volume of front-runners in this field; Ben Harvey rides for a trainer with a 0/1 T14 record, and at OR 120 she faces a class test against the top weights.

runners_data.name: Queenofthelodge
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 19f on Good for S Curling and Phillip Enright, and this is her quickest turnaround (8 days); she thrives on Good ground (13/15 sim-going) and is a genuinely front-running type who has been pushed back in the map — she is likely to try to push forward from the outset rather than settle where she is shown.

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Paddy is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with seven runners on Good ground over 2m2f, he is highly likely to dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop without serious pressure from another genuine pace-setter. Le Coq Hardi and Wild Bill Hickok are the primary prominent chasers who will sit closest behind, making this a race run to Shadow Paddy's rhythm rather than a contested, breakneck tempo. The field is notably packed with prominent-style horses — Court Canyon, Lady Bluebird, Queenofthelodge, and Soir De Garde are all natural front-runners or prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred berth and have been redistributed rearward in the mapping; of those, Court Canyon and Lady Bluebird are most likely to push forward and actually claim the positions nearest Shadow Paddy. A controlled, single-pace gallop that plays into the hands of horses capable of travelling fluently close to the leader and quickening off a sound jumping round favours the prominent-to-midfield runners with class and fitness — Shadow Paddy's front-running control and Le Coq Hardi's De Bromhead-trained quality look ideally placed in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shadow Paddy Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy sets an uncontested, honest gallop and jumps fluently throughout, dictating the tempo from the front.
scenarios.body: Shadow Paddy uses his class (OR 136, five wins on Good) to control the pace, making every fence on his own terms and stretching the field turning for home; horses who travel prominently and jump well are best positioned to challenge, while redistributed hold-up types lack the momentum to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy sets a genuine enough gallop that one of the prominent chasers — Le Coq Hardi or Wild Bill Hickok — has enough left to overhaul him at the last.
scenarios.body: Le Coq Hardi (OR 135, De Bromhead, 1-2 in last two over 2m on Good) tracks the pace with consummate ease and delivers a challenge at the final fence; Wild Bill Hickok, stepping up in trip from 2m, could also finish strongly if the early pace is sufficient to soften the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Runs Away
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy jumps brilliantly and the prominent chasers cannot sustain contact, leaving him to win unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Shadow Paddy's five-from-five win record on Good ground and a T14 strike-rate of 1/14 suggest an in-form yard capable of producing a peak performance; if the redistribution of Court Canyon and Lady Bluebird towards the rear means there is no real pressure at any stage, the front-runner can simply gallop rivals into the ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens mid-race and the front-running group tires, giving back-of-the-field types a run.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially undermined by the fact that the apparent hold-up runners — Queenofthelodge, Lady Bluebird, Soir De Garde — are true prominent types redistributed rearward and are unlikely to produce the sustained late runs of genuine closers; Soir De Garde (Mullins, OR 120, winner last time) is the best-credentialled if this freak shape does emerge.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Paddy's jumping accuracy is the critical variable — if he fiddles a fence and loses momentum, Le Coq Hardi is perfectly positioned to capitalise immediately.

Queenofthelodge and Lady Bluebird may both try to push forward from their mapped midfield positions in the early stages, creating brief traffic behind Shadow Paddy that could unsettle runners at the first few fences.
Wild Bill Hickok is unproven beyond 16f — watch for signs of him being asked for his effort earlier than ideal if the gallop is only modest and jockey Finegan misjudges the trip.

Soir De Garde's position in running is genuinely uncertain — Paul Townend is unlikely to accept a back-of-the-field role on a horse that has always raced prominently, so monitor where he actually lines up at the start.

Court Canyon's 87-day absence for a yard showing 0/9 in the T14 window means fitness must be taken on trust; he won fresh last time but the layoff combined with an overcrowded prominent group makes his race harder to read.

races.name: Guinness Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Flying Ace
runners_data.note: Four wins from his last five starts including three on Good, and Elliott has him primed with a 32-day freshener; a natural front-running type, he is likely to be squeezed off the pace by the surfeit of prominent horses and will have to work harder than ideal to find a rhythm.

runners_data.name: Midnight Jet
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old is the race's only confirmed front-runner, boasting a win at this course on Good ground and the significant luxury of leading without pressure; 80 days since last run is the one query, but he carries top weight with confidence.

runners_data.name: Brother Walfrid
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy rides for Elliott's powerful string and this horse arrives on the back of a Galway win on Good going, giving him obvious claims on form; he will want to race prominently but there are simply too many similar types, so he may find himself competing for a position he cannot always get.

runners_data.name: Look Sport
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's five-year-old is a single-run novice who won on Good over a shorter trip and has a hood listed; in this field he has been pushed back to the rear in the pace mapping, which genuinely suits him least — he is at his best racing positively and his inexperience adds risk.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's runner comes here race-fit after a 16-day turnaround and scored last time out on Good, but his record shows he has finished in the frame ten times in fifteen runs without dominating; he races prominently by nature but will need a clear run if the early positions fill quickly.

runners_data.name: Roc Dino
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Willie Mullins and this horse showed smart form when winning over 2m6f on Good, suggesting the trip and ground are in his favour; he sits in the prominent bracket but is the most likely to find a clean berth just off the pace and mount a serious challenge.

runners_data.name: Rosie's Wings
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's mare won her most recent start at Kilbeggan on Good and has run five times on that surface, building course-and-going confidence; though she wants to race forward, the congestion among prominent types means she is likely to be racing at less than her natural pace position, which will test her adaptability.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Carthage
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's gelding is lightly raced but has placed twice at Galway and won last time out on Good over an identical 2m4f trip, making the form and conditions a solid fit; he races prominently and, crucially, may find a gap given that he is not drawn into the same trainer cluster as the Elliott horses.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Jet is the one confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine pressure horse to challenge him for the lead, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m4½f trip on Good ground at Galway. Flying Ace, Brother Walfrid, Luker's Tipple, Rosie's Wings, and Look Sport are all natural prominent-running types, but with five such horses competing for three or four places in the first group, several will be unable to secure their preferred position and will be shuffled back against their nature. Midnight Jet therefore holds a significant tactical advantage — he can bowl along at his own tempo, conserve energy over jumps, and leave rivals in uncomfortable spots. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile, with Midnight Jet the primary beneficiary; any horse capable of travelling smoothly in second or third without fighting for position will also be well-placed, while those forced widest or deepest in the reshuffle face a stiffer task.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Midnight Jet Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Jet bowls along uncontested and sets a measured pace that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: He dictates from flag to finish on Good ground at Galway, jumping neatly and never coming off the bridle until asked in the straight; De Bromhead's charge has won on Good going and is proven at this level, making him the standout beneficiary of an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overcomes Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — most likely Flying Ace or Brother Walfrid — manages to slot into a forward position and tracks Midnight Jet closely enough to pounce.
scenarios.body: The early jostle for position resolves quickly and a genuine prominent horse travelling second or third gets a clean, economical round of jumping; Gordon Elliott's pair in particular carry strong recent form and their handlers will be keen to get them into the race early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Sets Up Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Jet's controlled tempo is genuinely slow enough that the race turns into a sprint from the last, bringing hold-up types into play.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the early stages compresses the field and a horse that has relaxed in mid-division delivers the strongest finish; Roc Dino, proven on Good and trained by Mullins, is the most credible beneficiary given his class and Paul Townend's ability to position from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At Pace: Prominent Collision
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to concede position and create a contested early pace that burns out the front rank.
scenarios.body: Increased fractions drain the leaders before the home turn and a more patient traveller finds openings in the straight; this is the least likely shape given Midnight Jet's clear front-running edge, but Siege Of Carthage and Roc Dino hold the strongest claims if attrition strikes.

watchPoints.text: Midnight Jet has a clear lead on tactical advantages but is 80 days off a run — watch the market for any late confidence signs from the De Bromhead camp, as freshness could cut both ways at this trip.

Flying Ace, Brother Walfrid, Luker's Tipple, and Rosie's Wings are all natural prominent types entering the same narrow channel — early crowding or bumping approaching the first hurdle could compromise multiple fancies simultaneously.

Roc Dino's Mullins/Townend combination at big-meeting Galway warrants attention; if he travels smoothly in a disciplined position behind Midnight Jet's controlled pace, he could prove the most dangerous late mover in a scenario that does not fully materialise into a cavalry charge.

Look Sport is a one-run novice equipped with a hood who faces a much more experienced field; monitor his starting price drift as a signal that connections are managing expectations against this level of opposition.

Siege Of Carthage has the specific course-and-distance win that makes him the dark horse if the pace scenario fractures — if the prominent cluster burns out, his Galway form becomes highly relevant at a potentially generous price.

races.name: Guinness Galway Hurdle Handicap (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Solness
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter at OR 153, JP O'Brien trained and ridden by JJ Slevin; 11 days since last run and has the tongue-tie, but the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing out of role as a Prominent type asked to lead — his chance depends heavily on whether he can conserve enough from the front on Good ground over 2m.|
runners_data.comment: Solness arrives here just 11 days after a placed effort — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back — showing he's in consistent form, and he has experience of today's trip and going. With a trainer firing at 28%, he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Casheldale Lad
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has strong course-and-distance form on Good ground (three wins at 2m-plus on this surface) and Josh Williamson's 5lb claim reduces his burden to a manageable 165lbs; 213-day absence is the one risk, but a horse with a genuine prominent style and Elliott's volume operation behind it is well-placed to track Solness.|
runners_data.comment: Casheldale Lad arrives here as a double winner in recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going — giving him a solid profile at 165 lb off an official mark of 152. The sole concern is a fall two starts back, though a close third last time suggests confidence is intact.

runners_data.name: Ndaawi
runners_data.note: Another Elliott prominent runner, has won twice at 2m on Good going and finished third in his last run 60 days ago; the 5lb claim for James Smith helps and his headgear (p) fits a horse that needs to be switched on — his recent Good-ground form reads well for the conditions but he was a beaten favourite at 17f soft last time, so the step back to a flatter test on Good is a plus.|
runners_data.comment: Ndaawi bounces back from an unplaced run with a win on his latest start, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat at 165 lb; the 60-day absence is the one query.

runners_data.name: El Cairos
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the saddle for Elliott lifts this horse's profile considerably; has hit the frame at 2m on Good going and his form figure of 4/16f/GOO is directly relevant — the F and 5 in recent form show vulnerability but Good ground at this trip is his comfort zone.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and fifth two starts back give El Cairos a modest recent profile, but a win three starts back shows he retains ability. He has experience over today's trip and going, though 93 days off the track is a fitness query at 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Laafi
runners_data.note: William Durkan's five-year-old has a single second on Good at 2m as his best going-relevant effort and his form string shows inconsistency (055D) before that second last time; the trainer's 0/4 strike rate in the last 14 days tempers enthusiasm and his prominent style means he will need to find space in a very busy early order.|
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, with a disqualification before that muddying the waters, Laafi has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 150 marks him out as a serious contender; the main concern is 82 days off the track carrying 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Puturhandstogether
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden riding for JP O'Brien after a 44-day break; recent form shows three figures of 16, 7 and 13 in his last three Good or Soft starts over trips longer than today's, and stepping back to 2m appears a positive — but the prominent style in a crowded race at his current OR of 140 looks like a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a second four starts back the lone highlight in a patchy recent sequence, Puturhandstogether returns after 44 days off carrying 153 lb; has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28% offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Tounsivator
runners_data.note: Only 3 days since his last run is a flag worth noting; Danny Mullins takes over for Willie Mullins and the horse has won twice on Good ground, most recently at 12f and 14f — the step to 2m is a query but his Good-going profile (12 runs, 4 wins, 5 places) is strong and he can race close to the speed.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning on just three days' rest, Tounsivator faces a stiff ask carrying 152 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 145 suggests he holds residual ability in a big field.

runners_data.name: Murcia
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins and this horse's true style is prominent, but the size of the field means he is mapped to midfield — he won at 2m on Good recently and his last run was just 14 days ago; the redistribution means he may be denied his preferred front-rank berth, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 tempers his prospects in a shape where he cannot dominate.|
runners_data.comment: Ran to some effect last time out with a second, and a winner two starts back keeps her profile alive, though she carries a hefty 151 lb and ranks seventh of 21 on our rating; has run over today's trip and going, but patchy recent form is the concern.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh for Mullins after just 3 days since last run; six consecutive figures of 6 in his recent form at 2m on Good and Yielding ground tells a consistent story of hitting the frame without winning — his prominent style fits the race shape but that record suggests a place at best.|
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner four starts back but has pulled up since and was beaten again three days ago; he has run over today's trip and the 151 lb burden won't help him make his way back from the top of that recent slide.

runners_data.name: Helvic Dream
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Noel Meade; his last five results include a run of 17th and 11th on Soft going, and his Good-ground record is better (sim-going 10/15 with 4 wins) — however, his natural prominent style is squeezed out in this field and recent form at this level has been poor, making him difficult to place competitively.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 143 suggests he holds ability. The 88-day absence and 149 lb burden are the key concerns.

runners_data.name: Starting Fifteen
runners_data.note: Sean Flanagan rides this five-year-old who won at 2m on Heavy (HEA) and finished second on Good — he handles the trip but his last run was 111 days ago and his natural front-running tendency is one that the map cannot accommodate; if he does not get a forward position he is unlikely to win from deep in a 21-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Starting Fifteen landed a win three starts back and was second four starts back, but fifth last time out suggests he returns here out of form; has run over today's trip and going, though 111 days off the track and 148 lb to carry are notable hurdles.

runners_data.name: Gameball
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old won twice at 2m on Good going and placed in his latest start 20 days ago; Darragh O'Keeffe rides and his form on this surface (4/5 in the frame) is excellent — as a natural prominent runner who may be shuffled back, he needs to assert early or his strong Good-ground record becomes irrelevant.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in recent starts, with a win four starts back and another five starts back, but he hasn't converted in his last three outings — a fourth, third, and runner-up. Has run over today's trip and going, and returns fit on 20 days' rest, though 146 lb is a stern burden.

runners_data.name: Ragmans Corner
runners_data.note: Won most recently at 17f on Good going and has form figures of 1, 2 and 4 on this surface — Eoghan Finegan takes the ride for Gerard Keane, a yard operating at 1/4 in the last 14 days; a natural front-runner compressed toward the middle of the field, he is the type who could force his way forward if the pace allows.|
runners_data.comment: Ragmans Corner won last time out and has distance and going experience in his favour, but ranked 19 of 21 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; 67 days off the track adds another question mark for the handicapper to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: Won at 17f on Good last time out and has multiple Good-ground wins; Daniel King takes the ride and at OR 129 he gets in light — his prominent tendencies pushed into midfield could turn into an asset if the race becomes congested and he is positioned on the better ground on the outer.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 17 of 21 on our figures, Putapoundinthejar faces a stiff ask under 142 lb, and his recent form is patchy — third and fifth in the two starts before that, though he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up type with strong recent form — won twice in three runs, the latest a second at 17f on Good; Brian Hayes for Mullins and at just four years old, still lightly raced over hurdles with a sim-going record of 3/7 including 1 win — his natural style suits a strong pace but that may not materialise, making this a ground-dependent watch.|
runners_data.comment: Beauvallon has winning form in recent starts — a winner two starts back and again three starts back — but ranked bottom of the field on our figures, he faces a stiff task conceding weight all round off 141 lb, despite arriving fit and with experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sageborough
runners_data.note: Conor Stone-Walsh for Paul Nolan; won at 17f on Good last time and is another natural prominent runner mapped rearward — the tongue-tie and Good-ground win record (2 wins in 5 on Good) are positives, but a trainer operating at 0/12 in the last 14 days is a cold flag in a race of this quality.|
runners_data.comment: Sageborough bounced back to winning ways last time out, but his last-five record is mixed — a fall and two out-of-the-money finishes among them — and 64 days off plus 141 lb make confidence hard to hold at a handicap mark of 128.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with six wins or places at this trip on Good going (sim-going 11/15); Danny McMenamin rides for Andrew Slattery, whose yard is live at 5/35 in the last fortnight — has genuine course-and-distance form but his true prominent style being pushed into the midfield mapping is a structural disadvantage in a field with this much pace.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Royal Hollow is hard to fancy despite a lively recent profile. She was a winner three starts back, and third two starts back, but 140 lb is a stern ask, and her rating of 127 leaves her well behind the top weights on paper; distance and going experience at least gives her a fair footing.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a 26-day break; hold-up style is genuine and Joshua Halford's 7lb claim helps on 140lbs — his recent form shows a single win at 16f on Heavy and a series of mid-division finishes, and on Good ground his one comparable run produced a 13th, making conditions a mild query.|
runners_data.comment: Barbizon has experience of today's trip and conditions, and a win in his last five starts gives him a platform, but back-to-back unplaced efforts are a concern; the 140 lb burden does him no favours here.

runners_data.name: Kai Lung
runners_data.note: Only 2 days since his last run is a major flag; Sean Cleary-Farrell's 7lb claim for the Mullins yard partially offsets 140lbs — his hold-up style is genuine (hg:h) and he placed at 2m on Good recently, but racing again after 48 hours makes him vulnerable to a fitness fade in the closing stages.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up and unseated in two of his last four starts before a third last time out, Kai Lung arrives 65 days fresh and is hard to fancy ranked 15 of 21 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and that sole recent win does at least show ability on a good day.

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim for Yvonne Latta, a yard with 0/0 in the last 14 days at the top level; his natural style is prominent but he is mapped rearward — has won at 20f and 23f, so 2m may be on the sharp side, and his recent form string includes a fall and a fourth, leaving questions about reliability at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 20 of 21 on our figures, Thisistheway is hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going; she does boast a win in her last five starts — five starts back — but a fall and a fourth in more recent outings make her a tough sell here.

runners_data.name: No Looking Back
runners_data.note: Trainer Oliver McKiernan has 0/3 in the last 14 days; genuine hold-up style with the tongue-tie and breast-girth, but his best recent effort was a third at 3m on
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled up and two unplaced efforts among recent form, No Looking Back is hard to fancy ranked 16 of 21 on our figures; 89 days off adds to the concern, though a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Solness is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 21-runner field, he can control tempo from the front without being pressured — a sustainable, owners'-pace scenario on Good ground at Galway. The field is loaded with horses that want to race prominently — Murcia, Helvic Dream, Starting Fifteen, Gameball, Ragmans Corner, Putapoundinthejar, Sageborough, Royal Hollow and others are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all get their desired position and will be shuffled back into midfield, meaning the race map overstates the contest for the early lead. With Solness able to bowl along unchallenged at a measured gallop, he sets a rhythm that neither shreds the field early nor invites a truly brutal finish, creating a race that develops into a stamina-test from three out rather than a sprint for home. The field's glut of frustrated prominent types compressed into midfield means closers must navigate traffic, and the tactical verdict is clear: horses capable of tracking the leader efficiently in the first two or three positions — true prominent or handy types who can secure a front-rank berth — are structurally advantaged, with genuine hold-up horses requiring a strong pace that simply may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solness Controls, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Solness dictates an uncontested lead at a fair gallop and the compressed midfield creates a traffic problem for late finishers.
scenarios.body: Solness rolls along in front without a serious challenger for the lead, conserving enough energy to repel challengers from the third-last, with handy types who tracked him from second or third benefiting most; Casheldale Lad and Ndaawi, both true prominent racers with the ability to sit just off the leader, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Hold Position
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed prominent horses manage to secure a forward berth closer to the pace than their mapped position suggests, creating a more contested early gallop.
scenarios.body: A busier early order develops as natural front-runners refuse to be buried, stringing the race out from an earlier stage and testing stamina on the Good Galway ground; horses with strong finishing kicks from just off the pace — Gameball and Ragmans Corner among those who manage to force their way forward — benefit from the faster tempo thinning the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from the home turn, stringing out the prominent pack and leaving a gap for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: Beauvallon, racing from off the pace under Brian Hayes for Mullins, and No Looking Back would need a strong gallop to drag them into contention, but the sustainable pace projection makes this a harder ask; this scenario is discounted because most of the field's supposed hold-up horses are actually displaced prominent types and the true staying-on closers lack the pace rating to overwhelm a well-managed front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Midfield Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield creates significant interference from three out, with a horse uniquely placed on the outer avoiding trouble and swooping late.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners funnelling down Galway's tight run-in, a horse produced wide and late — Putapoundinthejar or Sageborough, who have won at the trip on similar ground — could benefit if the inner is a congested meathook from the second-last; this remains the least likely shape because it depends on genuine pace horses actually acting like hold-up horses, but the sheer size of the field keeps it live.

races.name: Rockshore Refreshingly Irish Handicap

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a placed effort at 8f on Good ground; Stephen Thorne's yard is out of form over the last fortnight (0/9) and the 3lb claim of Jack Kearney will need to be delivered from deep, where this race shape offers limited help.
runners_data.comment: Pink Oxalis is our top-rated runner in a field of 17, and her second last time out — returned quickly after just 11 days — shows she's heading the right way. Winless in her last six, the weight of 140 lb from stall 12 is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Strictly a hold-up type who has placed at 7f on Good ground but has not won at this trip; Nicola Burns claims 5lb, trainer Gerard O'Leary has had limited recent ammunition, and a 22-day absence from a horse who typically races over shorter is a concern on the step up to 1m½f.
runners_data.comment: Tolebi has been knocking on the door, finishing fourth last time out and fourth again three starts back, and he has run over today's going before; 22 days between runs leaves him fit enough to threaten; the risk is he's yet to win in recent starts and that 137 lb burden could just blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Hygge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent recent form, winning over 8f on Good ground last time and placing over longer trips on similar surfaces; Gordon Elliott's yard is firing (4/30 in 14 days) and Declan McDonogh's booking is a strong positive — the trip and pace shape here suit ideally.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below his official mark on our figures and ranked near the foot of the field, Hygge is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 133 lb is a stiff ask for a horse rated this low on speed.

runners_data.name: Molto Amichi
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground most recently and has placed repeatedly on similar going; Luke McAteer rides and Eoin Griffin's yard has had limited recent winners, but this horse's profile of racing prominently and finishing cleanly on Good turf makes this pace scenario genuinely suitable.
runners_data.comment: Molto Amichi arrives on the back of a win last time out, with a second two starts back suggesting he's been in decent nick recently, though a ninth three starts back hints at inconsistency; he has run over today's distance and going, and 133 lb from stall 5 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Vega's Muse
runners_data.note: Tagged as racing slightly out of role in this field despite being the lone front-runner; the 33-day absence and a form string that includes a wide miss (8th) and a blank (0) around a win suggests reliability is not guaranteed, and at OR 83 she faces a stiff task if she cannot control the tempo precisely as she prefers.
runners_data.comment: Vega's Muse showed she can win when landing the spoils four starts back, but her two most recent efforts have been disappointing, and at 133 lb from stall 9 she faces a stiff ask, though she has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a tongue-tie who has placed at 7f on Good going; a 14-day turnaround is fine, but Adrian McGuinness's stable has been modest in form lately and a record of 0 wins and just 1 place from 6 recent Good-ground starts is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Exquisite Acclaim showed a flash of form with a third two starts back, but he has been winless in his last six starts and that sixth last time out is a concern; experience over today's distance and going helps, though he faces a stiff task from stall 13 off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over 8f on Standard and placed on Good; Ben Coen's booking lifts the profile, but a return just 7 days after his last run is notable — if the race produces clean air wide, his tactical flexibility becomes an asset.
runners_data.comment: Glyndwr shaped well with a third last time out, and a winner five starts back, he arrives on a quick seven-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going — the 131 lb burden is the one note of caution, but the overall profile makes him an appealing each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Follow Me
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a tongue-tie and visor combination; W J Lee rides and Ross O'Sullivan's yard has been quiet (0/12 in 14 days), while a 30-day absence and a form string featuring 9th, 8th and 3rd last time leave the profile patchy, though his Good-ground place at 10f is on point for the trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Follow Me does at least return here with experience of today's trip and going, and that third last time out offers some encouragement; however, 129 lb from stall 16 makes life harder for a horse ranked sixth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (three 2nds in last five) who is a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map due to the volume of closers in this field; the 9-year-old tongue-tie-and-blinker combination from Gavin Cromwell's yard (1/35 last 14 days) suggests he will need a stronger pace than Vega's Muse is likely to set to deliver his best.
runners_data.comment: Earls has been runner-up three times in recent starts yet remains winless, and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past fortnight is a concern; he has distance and going experience to draw on, though, and returns after 17 days off in reasonable shape on paper.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Won twice over 10f and 12f on Good ground recently and arrives here just 2 days after his last run, which is a potential concern; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield by redistribution, his staying form and Gavin Ryan's positional awareness give him each-way claims if the race develops any pace from halfway.
runners_data.comment: Merlin The Wizard brings back-to-back wins into this and has run over today's trip and going, yet he carries a testing 128 lb from stall 14 and an eighth two starts before those victories highlights some inconsistency in his recent record.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed at 8f on Good ground in each of his last three starts; trainer-jockey combination of Andrew Slattery riding for himself is unusual, and the 5-day turnaround is sharp, but his course-track profile of placing repeatedly here on Good ground is a clear positive.
runners_data.comment: Zaraahmando is winless in his last six starts and, ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, is hard to fancy at the weights; that said, he has run over today's trip and going before, and back-to-back thirds suggest he keeps finding the frame.

runners_data.name: Calm The Jets
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the finish, which is a meaningful concern in a race likely to become a sprint from two out; a 50-day absence makes this even harder to rely upon, and a form string of 9th, 8th, 0, 8th after his only win suggests he has not built on that success.
runners_data.comment: Calm The Jets won one from his last five starts, though two recent eighths and a ninth and an unplaced effort suggest consistency is the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 123 lb from stall two, and 50 days off means fitness is also unproven.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed three times in five runs at 8f on Good ground and is reunited with Nathan Crosse; a tongue-tie-and-hood combination from Adrian McGuinness's yard (3/27 in 14 days) and a 5-day turnaround suggest he is in consistent work — a pace shape that keeps him close to the leader is exactly what he needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, No More Porter has placed four times in that spell but also gone unplaced, and returning just five days after his latest effort raises freshness questions; he has run over today's trip and going, and the 122 lb burden from stall 11 adds little appeal at a ranking of 13 of 17.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: Prominent-type with a tongue-tie-and-hood combination from Dermot Weld's stable; has placed at 8f on Good ground and over 10f, so the trip is not a concern, but a form string featuring back-to-back single-figure finishes and a 14-day return gives pause — Weld's 2/11 recent strike-rate keeps the yard in consideration.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tachos does arrive with experience of today's trip and going, yet a fifth last time out is her best recent effort and a draw of 17 gives her plenty to consider from the off.

runners_data.name: Java Wood
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural front-end style means he is unlikely to get that position in a 17-runner field with this much pace; Wesley Joyce claims 3lb and the horse won over 8f on Good ground last time, but the 2-day turnaround and redistribution away from his preferred role temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Java Wood is hard to fancy at these weights, though he does boast a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before — small consolation from stall ten after a 48-day absence.

runners_data.name: San Aer
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded on the pace map; has placed at 8f on Good ground and Jamie Powell takes the ride, but a form string of 9, 0, 0, 0, 5, 2 over recent starts and an 8-year-old profile make this hard to advocate in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: San Aer has run over today's distance and going before, and an 88 rating — ranking him second of 17 — suggests he's significantly better than his official mark of 70 implies; the concern is that he's winless in his last five starts, so converting that promise into results remains the challenge.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that berth against faster-breaking rivals in this large field; the hood is new headgear for a 4-year-old who has placed at 13f and 12f on Good going, so the drop to 1m½f is a question, and Leigh Roche will need to adapt the tactics given the positional reality.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Cala Bonita has been largely disappointing in recent starts — two eighths sandwiching a pair of fourths since winning five starts back — and her profile makes her tough to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns fit enough on a 14-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Vega's Muse is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner handicap over 1m½f at Galway on Good ground, and with no obvious rival to challenge her early, she is likely to control the tempo from the front at a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a pressured or gruelling pace. The cluster of prominent types — Hygge, Molto Amichi, Zaraahmando, No More Porter, Tachos and Calm The Jets — will jostle for the early positions just behind her, creating a compact, relatively slow-run race up front that compresses the field through the first half. This field contains more prominent and hold-up horses than the map can physically accommodate: Java Wood and Cala Bonita are genuine prominent types but are unlikely to secure their natural positions in a field this large and competitive, while Merlin The Wizard, Earls and San Aer are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield by redistribution. A controlled, single-pace gallop set by Vega's Muse strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the leader — horses who can track the tempo, save ground and pounce in the straight — and disadvantages the genuine closers who need a strong pace to close from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vega's Muse Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Vega's Muse leads comfortably at a sustainable tempo with no rival applying pressure, allowing the prominent stalkers to race in a tight pack just behind.
scenarios.body: Vega's Muse controls the pace from the front and the field strings out in a single-file procession, leaving the horses positioned just off the leader — Hygge and Molto Amichi — perfectly poised to pounce in the straight where their recent form on Good ground counts most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out, rewarding horses with a sharp change of gear from a handy position.
scenarios.body: The compressed early gallop turns the contest into a dash home, suiting horses who have been ridden positively and can quicken from a prominent berth; Zaraahmando's consistent Good-ground placing form and No More Porter's repeated placed efforts at this trip profile make them ideal beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent types burn each other off faster than expected and a true hold-up horse threads through a tiring field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Merlin The Wizard has won over 10f and 12f on Good ground and, if racing closer to midfield than his natural position suggests, could find momentum late; Pink Oxalis also has a placed effort over 8f on Good ground and carries the profile of a horse who finishes strongly when the pace unfolds favourably.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Wide Draw
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding and traffic through the first bend causes the field to fan wide, handing an advantage to horses with tactical flexibility and clean air.
scenarios.body: A wide, strung-out field on Good ground at Galway over 1m½f can produce a flat-out gallop from home that suits horses who settle mid-division and travel well; Follow Me and Glyndwr both carry that profile and have recent Good-ground placed efforts to recommend them.

watchPoints.text: Hygge and Molto Amichi are the two horses best positioned to track Vega's Muse just off the pace — watch whether either can hold that slot through the first bend in a 17-runner field, as traffic at Galway over this trip can disrupt the best-laid plans.

Vega's Muse sets the key tactical variable for this entire race — if she is pressured or headed early by any of the prominent types scrambling for position, the pace could spike and turn the race into a genuine test that brings the hold-up horses back into contention.

Merlin The Wizard ran just 2 days ago and San Aer and Java Wood also return after 2-day turnarounds — watch the market for any drifts that suggest these horses are not at their sharpest after such quick returns.

Zaraahmando has placed at 8f on Good ground at this course in three consecutive runs — if he gets a clean run from his prominent position, he is the most consistent form-line in the race at his lower OR of 74.

The redistribution of Earls, Merlin The Wizard, San Aer, Java Wood and Cala Bonita away from their natural positions means the actual running of this race may look very different from the map — watch the early stages to see which of these horses concedes ground and settles further back than expected.

races.name: Guinness 0.0 Handicap

runners_data.name: Arch Enemy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two wins from two at Galway on Good, giving him strong course credentials; Gary Carroll is an intelligent booking in big-field handicaps where position is everything, and the 15-day turnaround looks fine.
runners_data.comment: Arch Enemy arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, though she carries 140 lb and sits mid-division on ratings — the earlier inconsistency in her recent form a reminder she's not always at her peak.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Prominent racer ideally suited to sitting just off a lone front-runner; 13 of his last 15 runs have been on Good ground demonstrating excellent surface reliability, and the 26-day break is no concern for this well-travelled five-year-old.
runners_data.comment: Autumn Twist arrives on the back of a third four starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 79 suggesting he holds solid claims as one of the leading dangers here; the risk is that he's been winless in his last five starts, and his latest ninth will need reversing.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who returned just two days ago and whose form string of six consecutive zeros on Good ground provides no encouragement; the fades-in-finish tag compounds concerns about his ability to land a blow in this stronger-than-usual company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Dark Summit nevertheless catches the eye through our rating of 83 — 13 lb clear of his official mark — and has experience of today's going; the risk is that his recent sequence of unplaced efforts is hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Genuine closer who has placed twice from hold-up berths at this sort of trip on Good, including a second over 13f; in a race with so many hold-up horses fighting for rear positions, she may find herself squeezed for space — a concern in a 21-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Justenzia does carry an encouraging rating edge over her official mark, yet consecutive unplaced efforts are a concern; two seconds in recent starts show ability, and she has run over today's trip and going, though 140 lb is no aid.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who specialises in longer trips (16-20f typically) and may find this 1m4f slightly sharp; however Gavin Ryan's experience in big Galway handicaps is an asset, and 14 of 15 runs have been on Good ground so the surface is absolutely fine.
runners_data.comment: Pahlavi arrives here with experience over today's trip and going, and a second three starts back followed by a third four starts back gives him a solid recent profile — our rating of 88 heads the field. Yet to win in his last four starts, and a trainer in lean form are the notes of caution.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Likeable hold-up performer with recent Good-ground wins at 10f and 12f showing the trip suits; Gary Carroll's booking (here on Arch Enemy, so this is Adam Caffrey's charge — Gary on Arch Enemy) — notably won on Good last time out and has course form, making him a live danger if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Annie's Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces who has repeatedly placed at 16f on Good ground, suggesting she handles the conditions and stays well; struggling to convert on the bigger stage but the trip and going suit, and Adrian McGuinness has been in form recently (3/27 over 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Placed second five starts back but winless in recent starts, Annie's Angel returns after 24 days with experience of today's distance and going in her favour — our rating of 79 ranks her third of 21, though her last three runs have been modest.

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Standard recently and has placed at 9f and 12f, showing versatility around this sort of trip; Jack Kearney (3lb claimer) reduces his weight burden and his prominent style is ideally suited to stalking Oust from second or third.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, Baila Conmigo is hard to fancy at the weights, though he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Berto Ramirez
runners_data.note: His natural instinct is to race from well off the pace and finish late, but with so many closers in this field he is unlikely to find the backmost berth he needs; his one win at 18f on Good shows he stays, but being forced closer than ideal takes the edge off his profile here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 52 days, Berto Ramirez arrives with obvious questions to answer, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 76 suggests a shade more ability than his official mark of 69 credits him with.

runners_data.name: Speckled Meadow
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist who won over 12f on Good but whose form string of 6-5-6-8-23 shows declining returns; at OR 69 and carrying 139lbs, the weight and age are challenges in a competitive 21-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Speckled Meadow nevertheless has experience of today's trip and going, and 16 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh; however, a weight of 139 lb looks a tough ask for a mare ranked eighth of twenty-one.

runners_data.name: Day Trader
runners_data.note: Confirmed closer who has raced in rear positions throughout his career, but his actual run positions — 10th, 14th, 16th — reveal limited ability to improve late; shuffled into the midfield depiction here because the rear is oversubscribed, though his true role is deep hold-up, and he has never won off a mark this competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with unplaced efforts dominating recent form, Day Trader is hard to fancy from a ranking of 19th of 21 on our figures; the 33-day absence offers no obvious excuse, and the 138 lb burden adds further pressure.

runners_data.name: Rhythm King
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who finished only two days ago and whose form figures of 5-5-0-0-6 on any combination of ground shows minimal ability to land a significant blow; racing out of his natural deep-rear position in this busy field further undermines his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 276 days, Rhythm King faces an obvious fitness query on his return; he has run over today's going before and a speed rating of 90 offers some encouragement, but recent form has been uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Western Bandit
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and prefers to stalk from just off mid-division, but his form of 0-5-7-7-3 on Good with a preferred trip around 8-10f raises genuine questions about whether 1m4f will stretch his stamina; pushed away from his natural racing position in this packed field, that distance concern looks significant.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, Western Bandit does bring going experience and a fitness edge at 19 days since his last run, though a third two starts back is the only bright spot in a patchy recent sequence, and 138 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Faro Island
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and has placed twice from a prominent-chasing role; W.J. Lee is a top booking for a race like this and his consistent Good-ground form over 10-12f suggests the 1m4f step is the only question — he is interesting at what may be a decent price.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and seventh the run before that make Faro Island hard to fancy despite a win three starts back; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, the evidence points firmly against him.

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: Has placed in four of her last six runs including seconds and thirds at 11f and 12f on Good, showing genuine consistency; her true running style is closer to hold-up than her mapped position, meaning in this congested rear-of-field scenario she will need a gap to appear, but her form credentials are hard to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts but consistently finding the places of late — third last time out and a second two starts back give her solid each-way claims; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 19 days since her last run leaves her reasonably fresh, though 136 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Lily Parr
runners_data.note: The 73-day absence is a notable concern in a competitive flat handicap, as is the fades-in-finish flag; her actual running style is hold-up and she is shifted forward on the map merely because of overcrowding at the rear, so her chance should be treated with caution on both fitness and style grounds.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and 73 days off the track, Lily Parr faces a stiff ask off 136 lb, yet she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating edges above her official mark, suggesting a shade of unexploited potential.

runners_data.name: Oust
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner on just 129lbs — a significant weight advantage in a field of older horses carrying 135-140lbs — who has been placed twice in six runs on Good ground around this trip; his ability to control tempo without pressure is the defining pace factor in this race, and his light weight makes him dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back and a third four starts back hint at ability, and he returns after 23 days with experience over today's trip and going; the concern is back-to-back seventh and sixth finishes suggest he's struggling to recapture that form.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Has won twice from hold-up positions on Good ground recently (over 11f and 10f), giving him a strong form case; Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard has been firing (16/67 over 14 days) and the three-year-old allowance helps, though being denied his preferred deep-closing berth in this congested field is the obstacle to his chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying 127 lb, Rodeo Blues faces a stiff ask, though her back-to-back wins heading into this represent genuine recent form. She has experience of today's going, and a trainer firing at 28% over the last fortnight offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Quiz Test
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three consecutive placed efforts at 14-17f on Good, suggesting he handles conditions and stays strongly; no jockey listed is a concern from a betting perspective, but his consistent form profile over longer trips on this ground makes him quietly interesting stepping back from those extreme distances.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 17 of 21 on our figures, Quiz Test faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out offers slim encouragement, but 50 days off and 136 lb make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Has won twice in recent starts (over 10f on Standard and 8f on Heavy) and wears a hood; his natural running style is hold-up but forced into midfield depiction because the rear is oversubscribed — his wins have come on faster-surface types, and Good ground over 1m4f is unproven, making this a step into the unknown.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Blackjack Hills faces a stiff ask, but he does bring experience of today's distance and going and ran second last time out — a genuine bright spot in a mixed recent record.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Soft and placed twice over 12f on Good and Soft, showing she handles cut conditions; wears a hood and her instinct is to race from off the pace, but like many rivals here she cannot occupy her natural rear position in a 21-runner field — the Good ground (rather than Soft) is also a mild concern given her preference.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in her last three outings — sixth, fifth, and eighth — Nancee Spain's sole recent win came four starts back, and she ranks 15th of 21 on our figures; distance and going experience offer some hope, but she's hard to fancy from this profile.

races.paceDynamic: Oust is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure from any other confirmed lead type, meaning he can control tempo at a comfortable, sustainable clip over 1m4f on Good ground at Galway. With only one horse confirmed to dictate, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which classically favours those racing just off the leader in the prominent or close-midfield positions who can travel without expending energy early. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can physically place at the rear — Berto Ramirez, Western Bandit, Rodeo Blues, Jujubella, Nancee Spain, Blackjack Hills and Day Trader among others are genuine closers shuffled into a midfield depiction because the rear cannot accommodate them all, meaning true late closers will be harder to find and their chances are structurally compromised. This race shape decisively favours prominent racers who can sit within two or three lengths of Oust, avoid cover problems in a large field, and kick from the front of the chasing pack in the straight — horses like Autumn Twist, Baila Conmigo, Annie's Angel and Faro Island fit this profile best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oust Leads, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Oust sets a controlled, even tempo and horses racing prominently just off the pace travel sweetly before asserting in the Galway straight.
scenarios.body: Oust's lone front-running role allows the pace to be metronomic rather than fierce, giving the prominent chasers like Autumn Twist and Baila Conmigo an ideal engine room to work from without burning energy; in a 21-runner flat handicap on Good ground, those who secure a berth in the first five or six and avoid traffic will be best placed to exploit the modest gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Oust Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Oust's controlled front-running translates into a genuine stamina-based solo performance and nobody in the prominent group has the class to reel him in over 1m4f.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure forcing Oust to burn himself out, he could effectively time-trial his way around and find rivals flatfooted when trying to close in the straight on Good ground; a three-year-old carrying only 129lbs, he has a significant weight advantage over older rivals and his recent placed form around this trip on similar ground supports the case.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just quick enough to string the field out and a resolute hold-up type punches through gaps in the straight before the prominent horses tire.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger pace than expected, or a prominently-ridden horse burning out, would open a gap for a midfield racer finishing with purpose; Rodeo Blues has the form profile to benefit here, with two recent wins from the back of midfield on Good ground, while Jujubella's consistent placed form also makes her a candidate if the race develops into a true test of stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Wide Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 21 causes severe congestion on the turn and several prominent types interfere with each other, leaving only horses who were wide or have clear runs to finish.
scenarios.body: In a 21-runner handicap over 1m4f at Galway, traffic incidents on the sweeping bend are a genuine possibility and could neutralise the prominent brigade entirely; horses with patient jockeys who take wide routes — such as Showyoutheropes or Arch Enemy who both have recent form at this course and over this trip on Good ground — could benefit from clear air.

watchPoints.text: Oust's weight advantage of 9-11lbs over most rivals is stark in a flat handicap — if Jimmy Dalton (7lb claimer) gives him a dream lead, his light burden could be decisive over rivals carrying significantly more.

With 21 runners, the turn into the Galway straight will be heavily congested — horses drawn wide or forced wide early may lose several lengths at a critical point, and any prominent racer who loses their pitch in the bunching will find recovery almost impossible.

Rodeo Blues and Jujubella both have strong recent form but are denied their natural deep-closing positions by field overcrowding — watch whether either jockey opts to take a genuinely wide route to secure clear air, as that is the only way their closing kicks can be deployed effectively.

Denis Gerard Hogan saddles three runners (Dark Summit, Justenzia, Autumn Twist) — Autumn Twist is by far the most interesting of the trio on form and style grounds, but the presence of multiple stable runners may affect race tactics if they are ridden in concert.

runners_data.name: Colga Boys
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Colga Boys returns quickly nine days after his latest unplaced effort, carrying 168 lb, and with so little form on the book he remains open to considerable improvement yet to win.

runners_data.name: Colliers Quay
runners_data.comment: Colliers Quay is lightly raced and unexposed, with a third two starts back offering the most encouraging note in a mixed profile; yet to win, he returns after 109 days carrying 168 lb and remains open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Gusserane
runners_data.comment: Gusserane arrives here 59 days since his last start, lightly raced and open to improvement, yet his last three outings include two pull-ups that demand explanation before backing him with confidence — he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Macdonagh Park
runners_data.comment: Macdonagh Park is unexposed and open to improvement, though yet to win in his last four starts, with that second two runs back the brightest glimpse of potential; returning after 90 days and carrying 168 lb, he remains one to keep an eye on as he develops.

runners_data.name: Market Square
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement after just one run on record, Market Square was fifth last time out and returns after an 89-day break carrying 168 lb — yet to win but lightly raced enough to leave the door open.

runners_data.name: Martymill
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, Martymill shaped with some promise when second last time out and, fresh after 59 days off, he returns carrying 168 lb with enough in the locker to suggest further improvement is possible.

runners_data.name: Mister O Reilly
runners_data.comment: Mister O Reilly returns after a 364-day absence carrying 168 lb, yet to score in recent starts and lightly raced enough to leave room for improvement; an open profile that makes him genuinely hard to assess on a comeback.

runners_data.name: Monard Flyer
runners_data.comment: Unexposed after just the one start — an eighth last time out — Monard Flyer returns after 65 days and remains yet to win, but with so little form on the book he's open to considerable improvement carrying 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Our Sonny
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and not seen for 418 days, Our Sonny returns carrying 168 lb as a lightly raced gelding with plenty still unexplored; that lengthy absence demands respect but leaves him open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Run Ted Run
runners_data.comment: Unraced and an unknown quantity on debut, Run Ted Run arrives carrying 168 lb — unexposed and with improvement entirely possible as connections learn what they have on their hands.

runners_data.name: Sir Vinny
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last two starts but has shaped with promise, finishing third two starts back and runner-up last time out — an unexposed gelding who looks open to further improvement carrying 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Dieux Diligence
runners_data.comment: Unexposed after just one start to his name, Dieux Diligence returns after 54 days with a yard operating at a sharp 28% strike rate behind him — the gelding is yet to win but remains open to significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Flashy Fred
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has finished second, second, and third in his last three starts, Flashy Fred arrives here on a sharp 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going — winless in recent starts but his placed record makes him the one to beat in this field.

runners_data.name: Gruncle
runners_data.comment: Gruncle makes his debut here carrying 164 lb, unexposed and open to any amount of improvement — a gelding about whom little is yet known, but that very inexperience leaves plenty of scope.

runners_data.name: Burning Like Fire
runners_data.comment: Burning Like Fire shaped with promise on her sole recent start, finishing third, and as a lightly raced filly she remains open to improvement. The 123-day absence is worth noting, but unexposed types like her can leave that form behind quickly.

runners_data.name: Girl From The West
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement after just one start on record, Girl From The West was seventh last time out but remains lightly raced and yet to win; stepping out again 20 days later under 157 lb, she has more to offer.
